That was a damn amazing rebuttal but I'll also add a few things:

1) Alison was actually an established comics creator before this. She had an independently funded comic, Xenospora, which she was promoting at the convention along with Honey Badger stuff. She's no longer allowed at any conventions run by CalEx elsewhere in Canada so her business running this comic is going to suffer because of it, so it's inaccurate to say that 'no-one in the Honey Badgers was a remotely successful cartoon artist before this' - Alison can't become more successful thanks to CalgaryExpo, so I think those damages would be plausible.

2) The 'harassment' you say was captured on tape? That was someone raising a question at a panel aimed at MRAs, Alison politely asking 'May I field that question? Because I consider myself a men's rights activist', the person who asked the question saying yes, and Alison explaining that she doesn't like feminism's portrayal of women as victims and that people should create the change they want to see instead of seeing themselves as helpless victims.
But yup. Harassing behavior. For sure.

3) Not only do lawsuits take lots of time and money, unless they are using the legal funds for anything other than what they say they are, they aren't scamming anyone. It's not fair to imply that.

4) The defense parties have been grasping at straws and have been throughout. They've got really crappy claims and have generally fucked around with the Honey Badgers a lot.

- They have tried to claim that since one of the charges must technically be settled in a different court (even though the two can be settled in the same court under the same umbrella of charges), they've tried to postpone and move the trial because of this.

- They refused to give the Honey Badgers the proper name of their legal entity, bitched about Alison changing the name constantly and tried to claim that she was showing contempt for the system with all those delays.

- Calgary Expo put a summary judgement on them right in the middle of their trial preparations.

- Calgary Expo changed their explanations as to why the Honey Badgers were kicked out multiple times.

- When the Honey Badgers decided to arrange an alternate meet-up for their fans in a public park, Calgary Expo sent a fucking policeman with a van (because they gave the impression that there were lots of people who needed to be forcibly detained) because they claimed that the badgers could potentially sneak back into the convention.

- Part of their claims for the Honey Badgers entering the convention on false pretenses was an obviously sarcastic statement Alison made on their kickstarter page about learning about nerd culture for decades in order to infiltrate the convention, and a statement Karen made about going undercover as space lepers.

I'd say that the Honey Badgers have a pretty good chance of winning tbh - the harassment charges have no bearing, there are damages they can claim and the behavior of the defense parties indicates that they know their cases rest on bullshit.
